categories.title: Direction, Intent, and Scope
categories.truth: Direction becomes useful only when it can reject work, expose assumptions, and survive disagreement without becoming vague authority.

categories.title: Core Loops, Rules, and Mechanics
categories.truth: A mechanic is a contract between intent, legality, consequence, feedback, and future choice; missing any part weakens the loop.

categories.title: Prototyping, Iteration, and Vertical Slices
categories.truth: A prototype is valuable when it kills uncertainty, not when it looks like progress.

categories.title: Controls, Movement, Responsiveness, and Game Feel
categories.truth: Game feel is a closed perception-action loop; every unnecessary delay, ambiguity, or competing correction weakens trust.

categories.title: Cameras, Targeting, Framing, and Readability
categories.truth: A camera is an information allocator, not decoration; it determines what the player can know and comfortably act upon.

categories.title: Animation Architecture and Data Flow
categories.truth: Animation scales when many actions share one stable language of gait, phase, target, contact, and result.

categories.title: State Machines, Blending, Layering, and Motion Selection
categories.truth: No selector compensates for missing motion coverage; blending hides small gaps but magnifies bad semantics.

categories.title: IK, Motion Warping, Procedural, and Physics-Based Animation
categories.truth: Contact quality depends on semantics and constraints, not merely stronger IK; the system must know what is allowed to move.

categories.title: Combat, Interaction, and Multisensory Feedback
categories.truth: Impact feels strong when timing, resistance, consequence, and recovery agree; louder effects cannot repair a false outcome.

categories.title: Level Design, Encounters, and Spatial Flow
categories.truth: Space is a rule system: distance, visibility, topology, landmarks, and recovery determine which strategies can exist.

categories.title: Worlds, Systems, Procedural Content, and Reuse
categories.truth: Procedural content is a search problem with validators, not a magic content multiplier.

categories.title: AI, NPC Decisions, Navigation, and Group Behavior
categories.truth: Believable AI is not maximum intelligence; it is coherent goals, bounded knowledge, readable choices, and recoverable failure.

categories.title: UI, UX, Onboarding, and Accessibility
categories.truth: Accessibility is the removal of unnecessary barriers while preserving the intended decision, not a separate easy mode.

categories.title: Progression, Economy, Rewards, and Balance
categories.truth: Balance is a moving relationship among choices, information, time, and recovery—not one globally correct number.

categories.title: Audio, VFX, Lighting, Haptics, and Presentation
categories.truth: Presentation is strongest when each channel confirms the same meaning while remaining optional and budgeted.

categories.title: Art Integration, Assets, Rigs, and Content Pipelines
categories.truth: A strong asset pipeline converts artistic variation into validated data without erasing provenance or forcing one-off repairs.

categories.title: Performance, Memory, Loading, and Scalability
categories.truth: Performance is a budget-allocation and evidence problem; average FPS alone hides the frames that damage play.

categories.title: Code Architecture, Tools, Data, and Build Pipelines
categories.truth: Architecture earns its cost only when it reduces the cost and risk of the next change.

categories.title: Multiplayer, Prediction, Replication, and Local Co-op
categories.truth: Networking is distributed agreement under delay; responsiveness comes from safe prediction, not from weakening authority.

categories.title: Testing, Telemetry, Debugging, Release, and Continuous Improvement
categories.truth: The first wrong frame, state, or decision is more useful than the final visible failure.

modules.title: Name the Player Promise
modules.shortcut: Write one sentence describing what the player repeatedly gets to feel or do. Use it to accept or reject features.
modules.rationale: A promise is easier to test than a genre label; “outsmart a living city together” guides more decisions than “open-world co-op.”
modules.guard: Do not turn the sentence into marketing fog. It must imply observable play.
modules.purpose: Turn “Name the Player Promise” from a one-off suggestion into a reusable, observable capability within product direction and design governance.
modules.problem: Without an explicit pattern, the project can drift through this failure chain: vague promise → locally reasonable features → conflicting systems → expensive polish on the wrong experience.
modules.operatingRule: Write one sentence describing what the player repeatedly gets to feel or do. Use it to accept or reject features.
modules.minimumApplication: One bounded application to one feature, mechanic, or project decision, with a captured baseline, explicit owner, one representative test, and a rollback-ready evidence packet.
modules.authorityBoundary: may guide decisions but must not silently redefine the project promise or promote itself to canon
